headline: Medium risk: Botpress can ingest PDF.js outputs without isolation, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error pathways; no direct data-leak or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls, while pdf.js processes PDF files and can surface document content into downstream workflows. That creates a plausible default pathway where attacker-controlled PDF text is treated as instructions by Botpress. The pairwise interaction is inferred from docs-only evidence, so uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is copied or forwarded into Botpress conversation context
IF Botpress treats file-derived text as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of PDF text into Botpress prompts
Add a provenance tag to all pdf.js-derived content
Require a human review step before Botpress acts on PDF-derived instructions
Restrict Botpress to a separate workspace from PDF processing
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and instruction-stripping before handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have network_egress set to none, and the profiles do not show shared credentials or a shared workspace. pdf.js touches PDF documents, but Botpress lists no data classes touched and no file surfaces. A leakage path is therefore not evidenced beyond a weak local handoff risk, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are run on the same local workspace with shared files
IF PDF contents include sensitive data and are manually copied into Botpress
mitigations: Keep Botpress and pdf.js in separate directories
Avoid copying PDF contents into chat prompts
Use redacted PDFs for testing
Verify no shared cloud sync or shared account is enabled
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation or per-agent storage separation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, and pdf.js supports multiple instances and browser-based tests, but neither profile shows unrestricted filesystem write, git mutation, or overlapping mutable scopes. The main conflict is limited to operational contention if both are run in the same environment, which is not documented as default. That makes the blast radius small and the pathway unusual.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same working directory
IF package installation by Botpress modifies files that pdf.js test runs also use
mitigations: Run each agent in its own directory
Pin dependencies before starting either agent
Avoid concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js can produce extracted document text, and Botpress is a conversational agent likely to consume that text in support workflows. If Botpress treats pdf.js output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations in extraction can cascade into incorrect responses or actions. No verification step is documented in either profile, so the interaction is plausible in default use and merits medium severity.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is forwarded into Botpress without a verification step
IF Botpress uses extracted PDF text as the basis for user-facing answers
mitigations: Add a verification step before Botpress responds
Show extracted text with source-page references
Require human approval for high-impact answers
Log extraction confidence separately from answer confidence
requires-engineering: build a citation-checking pipeline between pdf.js and Botpress

E_compliance.rationale: The profiles do not identify regulated data classes, residency constraints, or retention differences. Botpress lists no touched data classes, and pdf.js only lists PDF documents without a compliance designation. With no evidence of PHI, EU PII, or policy mismatch, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into the workflow
IF a deployment policy imposes residency or retention constraints not shown here
mitigations: Classify inputs before processing
Block regulated documents until policy review
Document retention settings for both agents
Separate compliance-sensitive workloads
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention
